variants.name: triton block-move hygiene
variants.mechanism: Single Triton _exp061_block_move_kernel with explicit 2D strides on both operands replaces every strided block move that PyTorch was running through its generic OffsetCalculator elementwise kernel (5002.9us / 107 launches / ~2.0 TB/s). The panel gather also subtracts the MXFP8 product and emits FP16 in the same pass, absorbing panel.sub_() and .to(float16); the solve-apply writes straight into the strided factor view via torch.mm(out_dtype=float32, out=...) so cuBLAS uses ldc=32768 and no scatter is needed; workspaces are allocated once per call. Arithmetic unchanged.

family.note: Those three families take _LARGE_FP8_FALLBACKS/_LEFT_LARGE_FALLBACKS on the ranked incumbent #906955 too (experiments/060-two-large-followup/combined-v1-familygrid.json, identical residuals to 3 s.f.). Not a regression.

variants.name: merged MXFP8 block-column update
variants.mechanism: Folds the diagonal block's TF32 SYRK into the panel's MXFP8 left-looking update as one block-column product. Both consume the same frontier factor[k:, :k] and the right operand factor[k:k+nb, :k] is its first nb rows, so _exp061_mx_column_product quantizes once and slices the right operand out of the same buffers -- quantized[:nb] for values and scales[: nb*cols//32] for the e8m0 scales, exact because _mx_quant_e4m3_blocked lays blocked scale tiles out row-tile-major. The 4733us TF32 SYRK at ~813 TFLOP/s disappears; the MXFP8 GEMM grows from 7.30e12 to 1.115e13 flops at ~2950 TFLOP/s; total quantized elements are unchanged at (n-k)*k.
variants.arithmetic_change: diagonal block SYRK moves from TF32 to MXFP8
variants.residual_margin_note: Dense residual moves 5.28 -> 6.44 of 20, so the margin tightens from 3.8x to 3.1x. Accepted by the orchestrator: 3.1x is the same order as what already ships on this shape and all six families still pass. Calibration point -- the sibling 1x16384 worker rejected an otherwise-faster variant that took its margin to 1.6x, and below ~2x this one would be rejected too. Any further variant that pushes the worst family past ~10 of 20 must be backed out.

invalid_evidence.cause: _exp061_move guarded on stride(1) == 1 and raised. torch.linalg.cholesky_ex(...).L is returned column-major (cloneBatchedColumnMajor), so its trailing stride is 4096. custom_kernel's safety chain swallowed the raise and the run measured the old _left_looking_cholesky_32768 fp8 path.
invalid_evidence.fix: kernel takes stride_src_m/stride_src_n/stride_out_m/stride_out_n and uses 64x64 tiles for a transposing move

not_attempted.diagonal_factorization: 11167us / 36.3% is cuSOLVER getrf_wo_pivot at ~0.34us/row. Sibling 1x16384 worker measured twelve blocked/recursive replacements, all slower than cuSOLVER, with 500x worse accuracy on the TF32 ones. Standing user directive also forbids new cuSOLVER-based fast paths and stream overlap. Left on the shipped call.

remaining_headroom: After V2 the shape is 24692us and cholesky_ex on the eight 4096x4096 diagonal blocks is 11167us of it (~45%), pinned at ~0.34us/row by cuSOLVER's serial panel cost. All remaining attackable overhead -- blocked inverse 1556us, fills 648us, triu_tril 458us, requantization 1021us -- sums to ~2.6ms, at most another ~1.12x.
